t: Royal Academy of Engineering Research Fellowships
desc: Five years of funding for early-career engineering researchers to build an independent research career.
note: Invited applications for the 2026/27 round close on 10 December 2026.
break_rule: Time for maternity or paternity leave, sick leave, caring or national service can be considered. The 2026/27 round also allows six extra months without a reason.
who: Early-career engineering researchers of any nationality, hosted by an eligible UK university or research organisation, up to four years after the PhD.

desc: Up to eight years of support for outstanding early-career scientists to become independent research leaders.
break_rule: Parental leave and sick leave over four weeks add the same time, up to six months. Caring, ill health and time outside research are also considered.
who: Early-career natural scientists of any nationality, 3 to 8 years after the PhD, without a permanent or tenure-track post.

desc: Fellowships for early-career researchers who need a flexible working pattern, for example because of caring responsibilities.
break_rule: Parental leave or sick leave over four weeks adds the same time, up to six months. Part-time work counts pro rata.
who: Natural scientists of any nationality without a permanent post, up to six years after the PhD, who need flexible support because of parental or caring duties or a health condition.
note: The Royal Society page currently shows the scheme as closed. Check the next round on the official page.

desc: Two years of funding for international postdoctoral researchers to come and work in the UK.
break_rule: Parental leave or sick leave over four weeks adds the same time, up to six months.
who: Non-UK citizens working outside the UK in the natural sciences, with at most five years of full-time postdoctoral experience.

desc: Three-year fellowships giving early-career researchers time to build an independent line of work.
break_rule: You can ask for an exception to the four-year limit for maternity, family commitments, illness or disability.
who: Researchers with a UK degree or UK academic post, within four years of submitting the PhD, without a permanent full-time academic post.

desc: Long-term support for early-career researchers and innovators across all UKRI disciplines.
break_rule: There is no time limit. You can list career breaks without giving reasons, and the panel takes them into account.
who: Early-career researchers and innovators moving to independence at an eligible UK organisation, with or without a PhD.

desc: All open UKRI calls, including EPSRC fellowships and new investigator awards. Filter by council and career stage.
Three-year fellowships for early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences.
break_rule: The three-year window after the viva can be extended for maternity leave, illness or family commitments, if agreed with the British Academy before applying.
who: Early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences, within three years of the viva, with a UK doctorate or a strong link with UK academia.

desc: Three-year fellowships for early-career scientists and engineers with exceptional research potential.
break_rule: Career breaks are not counted in the three-year limit, and parental or sick leave can extend the fellowship.
who: Science and engineering researchers with up to three years of postdoctoral experience who move to an approved UK institution.

desc: European fellowships for postdoctoral researchers to move country and develop new skills.
who: Researchers of any nationality with up to eight years of research experience after the PhD, who move to another country for the fellowship.
break_rule: Career breaks and time outside research are not counted in the eight years.

desc: Up to five years of funding for researchers up to 10 years after their PhD to lead their own team.
who: Researchers of any nationality with a PhD defended 0 to 10 years before 1 January 2027, working at least half time in Europe on the project.
break_rule: Mothers add 18 months per child, or the actual leave if longer. Documented paternity or parental leave, long illness and clinical training are also added.
note: From the 2027 call the time limit changed to 0 to 10 years after the PhD (before, 2 to 7).

desc: Funding for early-career researchers to develop their research identity, including in data science and health.
break_rule: Part-time work, parental leave, long-term sick leave and time outside research are taken into account.
who: Researchers with a PhD, or four years of research experience, and up to three years of postdoctoral experience, in the UK or an eligible low- or middle-income country.

desc: Funding for mid-career researchers to lead an ambitious research programme.
break_rule: A career break, parental leave or illness can exempt you from the rule that a permanent post must have started in the last three years.
who: Mid-career researchers in any discipline who already lead their own research, in the UK or an eligible low- or middle-income country.

desc: Postdoctoral fellowship for scientists who want to pivot to a new field. Candidates are nominated by their university.
who: Science, engineering, mathematics or computing PhDs who complete the PhD between 1 May 2026 and 30 June 2027 and are nominated by a partner institution.

desc: Fellowships for researchers returning to research after a career break of two years or more, for example for family or caring reasons.
who: UK residents with a research doctorate or three years of research experience, returning after a break of two years or more.
break_rule: The scheme is for people on a research career break of at least two years for family, health or caring reasons.

t: L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science, UK and Ireland
desc: Awards for early-career women scientists in the UK and Ireland. Funds can be used flexibly, for example for equipment, childcare or travel.

t: L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards
desc: International awards recognising women scientists for their research achievements.
Awards from the British Federation of Women Graduates for women in the final year of a doctorate.
Support for PhD students in computer science and related fields. Students are nominated by their university.
Advance HE leadership development designed specifically for women in higher education.
Framework and toolkits for advancing gender equality in higher education and research.
A structured map of researcher skills with planning tools for every career stage.
Community writing sessions that build momentum through focused, shared writing time.
Free, confidential emotional support and counselling for everyone working in education.

t: Maternity and parental leave in academia
desc: Plain-language guidance on rights, leave and flexible working for academic parents.
Research-led guidance on tackling staff-to-student sexual misconduct in higher education.
A competition that builds skills in communicating research clearly to a wide audience.
Government grant for practical support at work for disabled people and people with a health condition, such as equipment, support workers or travel.
Support for disabled students, including postgraduate researchers, to cover study-related costs.
UK visa route for leaders and potential leaders in academia and research, including holders of many major fellowships.
Organisation supporting Black students and researchers in UK higher education, with reports, events and research career programmes.
Charity supporting LGBTQ+ people in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, including the international LGBTSTEM Day.
Advice and support for people with caring responsibilities, including rights at work and flexible working.
Advance HE framework to improve the representation and success of minority ethnic staff and students.
Global community increasing the presence of Black people in artificial intelligence, with mentoring and workshops.
UK community for Black professionals and researchers in data, with events and career support.
Community of queer researchers in AI, with grad application support, scholarships and workshops.
Visibility campaign sharing the stories of LGBTQ+ people in STEM.
Support for academics in danger or exile, including fellowships at UK universities.
Free legal advice on parental leave, flexible working and caring rights at work.
Community and annual workshop for women and non-binary people in machine learning, with travel grants.
Global organisation for women in computing, home of the Grace Hopper Celebration and scholarships.
How funded PhD places work in the UK and where to find them, including doctoral training centres.
Search engine for funded PhD projects and studentships in the UK and abroad.
Government loan towards fees and living costs for a PhD, for students without full funding.
Government loan towards fees and living costs for a Master's degree.
Free programmes, mentoring and events for young women and non-binary people in STEM.
Grants for disabled students, including postgraduate students, to cover the extra costs of disability.
UK government scholarships for international students to do a one-year Master's in the UK.
Scholarships for students from Commonwealth countries to study for a Master's or PhD in the UK.
Up to five years of funding to consolidate an independent team and research programme at a host in Europe.
who: Researchers of any nationality with a PhD defended 5 to 15 years before 1 January 2027.
break_rule: Mothers add 18 months per child, or the actual leave if longer. Documented paternity or parental leave, long illness and clinical training are also added.

desc: A personal grant of up to 320,000 euros for recent PhD holders to develop their own research at a Dutch institution.
who: Researchers from the Netherlands or abroad who obtained their PhD within three years of the round's reference date.

desc: Short research stays in Germany, from 2 to 12 months for PhD students and 2 to 6 months for early postdocs.
who: Advanced PhD students and junior researchers at UK or Irish universities, including postdocs up to four years after the doctorate.

desc: A fellowship of 6 to 24 months for a research project with a host of your choice in Germany.
who: Researchers of any nationality and discipline up to four years after the doctorate.
break_rule: Fellows with children can ask to extend the fellowship and receive family allowances.
note: Selection committees meet in March, July and November. Apply four to seven months before.

desc: A three-year researcher contract and project funds at an Italian state university, for researchers working abroad.
who: Researchers with a PhD obtained 3 to 6 years earlier who have worked abroad for at least three years.
note: There is no fixed yearly date. The latest results were published in July 2026.

desc: Funding to lead an independent junior research group at a German university or research institution.
who: Postdocs with 2 to 4 years of experience after the doctorate and substantial international research experience.
break_rule: Women add two years per child and men one year per child, up to six years. Part-time work for childcare counts proportionally.

desc: A three-year postdoctoral project at an Austrian research institution, carried out with an Austrian mentor.
who: Early-career postdocs in any discipline up to five years after the doctorate, including applicants from abroad.
break_rule: The FWF says career interruptions should not be a disadvantage, but no fixed extension is stated.

desc: Grant towards extra care costs, such as childcare or respite care, so that members can attend physics events.
who: Members of the Institute of Physics who need additional care to attend a physics conference, meeting or event.
note: Apply up to four weeks before the event.

desc: Contribution to caring costs so that parents and carers can attend conferences, research schools or research visits in mathematics.
who: UK-based mathematicians with caring costs, with priority for early-career applicants. PhD students need a support letter from their department.
note: Non-members need an LMS member to countersign. Four decision rounds a year.

desc: Grant for extra caring costs, such as childcare or respite care, when you attend a chemistry meeting, conference or training event.
who: Chemists with an active role in the event who have extra caring costs. Outside the UK and Ireland, three years of RSC membership are required.
note: Apply at least six weeks before the event.

t: Biochemical Society Care and Assistance Grants
desc: Help with extra costs of attending a Society event, including childcare, care for dependants, companion travel and accessibility needs.
who: Current members of the Biochemical Society at any level, from undergraduate to emeritus.
note: Apply by the event's early-bird deadline, or one month before the event.

t: Applied Microbiology International Carers Support Grant
desc: Support for childcare or dependant care costs while members take an active part in meetings, conferences or training events.
who: Full, Fellow or Associate members with at least 13 months of continuous membership who take an active part in the event.
note: Up to £60 a day. Apply at least six weeks before the event.

desc: Grant towards extra care costs so that you can attend meetings supported by the Royal Astronomical Society.
who: Anyone attending an RAS-supported event who has extra care costs.

t: The Physiological Society Grant for Carers
desc: Contribution to care arrangements so that members who are unpaid carers can attend Society meetings and workshops.
who: Members of more than one year, not Associate Members, who are unpaid carers. Preference for those presenting work.
note: Apply at least one month before the meeting.

desc: The government adds £2 for every £8 that working parents pay into an account for approved childcare.
who: Working parents with a child aged 11 or under, or 16 or under if the child is disabled.
amount: Up to £2,000 per child a year
note: Up to £4,000 a year if the child is disabled. Reconfirm eligibility every three months.

desc: Up to 30 hours of free childcare a week for working parents in England with children aged 9 months to 4 years.
who: Working parents living in England who meet the earnings rules, with a child aged 9 months to 4 years.
note: You can apply from when your child is 23 weeks old.

desc: UKRI-funded PhD students keep their stipend during maternity, adoption, partner and neonatal leave, and the studentship can be extended.
who: PhD students funded through a UKRI training grant.
note: Then 13 weeks at the statutory maternity pay rate. Partners receive two weeks of paid leave.

desc: Free and confidential search that matches people in financial difficulty with grants from more than 1,700 UK organisations.
who: People in the UK who need financial help with essentials or other costs.

desc: Queen Mary hardship fund that gives non-repayable awards to current students facing financial difficulty.
who: Current Queen Mary students on the London campuses. Postgraduate and international students can apply after an unforeseen change in circumstances.
note: Open for 2026/27. Postgraduate and international students apply by 9 July 2027.

desc: Listing of part-time academic and professional jobs in UK universities and research organisations.
who: Anyone looking for part-time work in higher education and research.

desc: European Commission portal with research jobs, PhD and postdoctoral positions across Europe.
who: Researchers at any career stage looking for positions in Europe.
note: There is no part-time filter. Search for part-time in the keywords.

desc: UK employees can ask for flexible working, such as part-time or changed hours, from their first day in a job.
who: Employees in the UK. Employers must deal with requests in a reasonable way.

desc: Eligible parents can share leave and statutory pay in the first year after a birth, adoption or surrogacy.
who: Eligible parents having a baby, adopting or using a surrogate, where both parents meet the criteria.
note: Up to 37 weeks of the leave can be paid.

desc: A four-year fellowship for early-career researchers of Black heritage in the natural sciences at a UK host organisation.
who: Researchers of Black heritage, including mixed Black heritage, with a PhD and less than 24 months of postdoctoral experience, and a link to the UK.
note: Includes relocation and visa costs.

desc: Oxford graduate scholarships for Black British applicants, covering course fees and living costs, including for doctoral study.
who: Graduate applicants who identify as Black British and give their ethnicity in the Oxford application.
note: Apply by your course's deadline in November, December or January.

desc: UCL PhD scholarships to address the under-representation of Black, Asian and minority ethnic research students, including in computer science.
who: Home-fee students. The latest published criteria named Black or Black British, Bangladeshi and Pakistani UK residents.
note: Six studentships across UCL in 2026/27. Check the criteria for the new round.

desc: PhD scholarships for Black heritage researchers in physical sciences, mathematics, materials and related subjects at the University of Manchester.
who: UK residents eligible for home fees who identify as Black, Black British or mixed Black heritage.
amount: Full fees and stipend for 3.5 years
note: Computer science is not among the eligible subjects.

t: Grand Union DTP studentships for Black British students
desc: ESRC doctoral studentships for Black British students in the social sciences at Oxford, the Open University and Brunel.
who: Applicants of Black or mixed Black ethnicity, ordinarily resident in the UK and eligible for home fees.
note: Two awards for 2027/28 entry. Apply by the deadline of the chosen university.

desc: PhD studentships in media, arts and humanities for Black British and British minority ethnic researchers, with a three-month placement.
who: UK residents who identify with any Black, Asian or other minority ethnic group, including Gypsy, Roma and Irish Traveller.
note: Up to two awards. Closes at 16:00.

desc: A leadership programme for racially minoritised staff in UK higher education, with action learning sets and an institutional sponsor.
who: Leaders from racially minoritised backgrounds in UK universities, booked through their institution.
note: Usually paid by the institution. The next cohort runs from February to June 2027.

desc: A career programme with a workshop, coaching and peer coaching for Black women in UK universities.
who: Women and non-binary colleagues of African, African Caribbean or mixed Black heritage who are academic or research staff, or PhD students, at a participating university.
note: Places are offered through each participating university.

desc: A one-year mentoring scheme for Black, Asian and minority ethnic staff at UCL, Queen Mary, King's, UAL, LSHTM and SOAS.
who: Staff at partner institutions who identify as Black, Asian, mixed or minority ethnic. Academic mentees are postdoctoral to lecturer level.
note: Queen Mary is a partner. Applications for 2026/27 are expected to open in November 2026.

desc: Network of the Association for Black and Minority Ethnic Engineers, with outreach, events, mentoring and leadership training.
who: Students and professionals from Black and minority ethnic backgrounds in engineering and technology.

t: Renters' Rights Act: overview for tenants
desc: Official guidance on the private renting changes in England from 1 May 2026, including rolling tenancies, rent increases and the end of section 21.
who: Private tenants in England.
note: England only. Older advice about fixed-term tenancies may now be out of date.

desc: How landlords must protect your deposit in an approved scheme, and what to do if they have not done so.
who: Tenants in England and Wales who have paid a deposit.
note: Your landlord must protect the deposit within 30 days of receiving it.

t: Prove your right to rent in England
desc: The documents or online share code you need to show a landlord before you can rent a home in England.
who: Anyone renting in England. The method depends on nationality and immigration status.
note: England only.

desc: Charity advice on paying a deposit, getting it back, unfair deductions and compensation if a deposit was not protected.
who: Private renters in England.
note: Shelter's free helpline and webchat are for urgent cases, such as the risk of losing your home within two months.

t: Shelter England: Renters' Rights Act changes
desc: Charity guide to the changes for private renters since 1 May 2026, covering evictions, rent increases and how to challenge them.
who: Private renters in England.
note: Rent can now be increased only once a year, with at least two months' notice.

t: Citizens Advice: renting from a private landlord
desc: Advice on searching for a private rental, the checks to make before paying and the documents landlords ask for.
who: People preparing to rent privately in England.
note: Do not pay any money without seeing the property first.

desc: Police advice on recognising rental scams and what to do if you have paid money to a fake landlord.
who: Anyone looking for a rental property, including people arranging housing from abroad.
note: Report Fraud replaced Action Fraud in December 2025.

desc: Queen Mary housing advisers help with private renting, including a property search, a contract reading service and a renting guide.
who: Queen Mary students renting privately.
note: Housing Hub, Mile End, +44 (0)20 7882 5555.

desc: Telephone advice from the UK Council for International Student Affairs on student visas, fee status and funding your studies.
who: International students and applicants in the UK.

desc: The working hours limits and work rules for Student visa holders during term time and vacations.
who: Students in the UK with Student immigration permission.
note: Usually up to 20 hours a week in term time for degree-level study. Part-time postgraduate students may not work.

desc: The healthcare surcharge you pay with a visa application, and how the amount is calculated.
who: Visa applicants, including students and their dependants.
note: Paid upfront for the whole visa, for example £1,552 for two years.

t: QMUL visas and international student advice
desc: Confidential advice from Queen Mary's international student advisers on visas, work, travel and money.
who: Queen Mary students, applicants and offer holders.
note: Ask through Ask QM or book a 15-minute online drop-in.

desc: Advice for international students facing unexpected money problems, covering fee options, hardship funds and charities.
who: International students in the UK with unexpected financial difficulties.
note: Speak to your university's international advisers first. Claiming public funds breaks Student visa conditions.

desc: Small grants for students whose funding for the final year has met unexpected difficulties.
who: Students enrolled at a British university, normally in the last year of their course.
note: Start with the online enquiry form.

desc: Small grants for education and training costs, such as exam fees and materials, for adults whose first language is not English.
who: Adults settled in the UK whose first language is not English, especially refugees and people seeking asylum.
note: No grants for PhDs.

desc: Queen Mary centre with training, funding guidance, careers support and community for PhD researchers, postdocs and new lecturers.
who: Queen Mary researchers, from the start of the PhD to about the second year of a first academic post.
note: It brings together the former Doctoral College and Researcher Development support.

desc: Confidential one-to-one careers appointments, workshops and resources on academic and non-academic careers.
who: Queen Mary PhD researchers and postdocs.
note: PhD students book through the QM Careers Hub. Postdocs first email careers@qmul.ac.uk.

desc: National agreement on what researchers can expect from employers and funders on culture, employment and career development.
who: Researchers employed by signatory organisations, including Queen Mary.
note: Queen Mary encourages postdocs to spend at least 10 days a year on professional development.

desc: One-to-one mentoring that matches women engineers with independent mentors for twelve months.
who: Women engineers at any career stage.
note: Free for WES members, £120 a year for other mentees.

desc: BCS network that matches members in computing and IT with mentors by sector and skills.
who: Members of BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT.
note: BCSWomen members use this network.

desc: Members' mentoring programme that connects people with mentors outside their workplace.
who: Members of the Royal Society of Chemistry.

desc: BCS group with networking, events and career resources for women in computing and IT.
who: Women in computing and IT, through BCS membership.
note: Some webinars are free.

desc: One-day UK conference with a poster contest for women and non-binary students of computing.
who: Women and non-binary undergraduate and MSc students of computing in the UK.
note: The 2027 edition is on 8 April at the University of Birmingham. Bursaries usually cover travel.

desc: Network of women engineers with an annual conference, awards and International Women in Engineering Day.
who: Women in engineering, technology or science at any stage, including students. Others can join as supporters.
note: A free Supporter option includes the monthly newsletter.

desc: Global community with a yearly conference, regional events, a datathon and resources for women in data science.
who: Students and professionals interested in data science.
note: Check the events page for London dates.

desc: ACM council for women in computing, with chapters, events and scholarships to attend research conferences.
who: Scholarships are for students who identify as female and want to attend a computing research conference.
note: Contact acm-w-scholarship@acm.org for amounts and dates.

desc: International celebration of women in science, technology, engineering and maths, with events about role models.
who: Anyone can take part or organise a local event.
note: Held on the second Tuesday of October.

t: Women in HPC, N8 CIR chapter
desc: UK chapter of Women in High Performance Computing, with workshops, talks, mentoring and regular open meetings.
who: Anyone interested, by joining the mailing list.

desc: Confidential Queen Mary service with counselling, mental health and wellbeing advice, and specialist advisers for students affected by sexual assault or harassment.
who: Queen Mary students, and people supporting a student.
note: Phone lines are currently closed. Book through AskQM. Reception Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 16:00, Geography building, Mile End.

desc: Telephone helpline for Queen Mary students with emotional support and practical guidance when university services are closed.
who: Queen Mary students.

desc: Confidential support for Queen Mary staff, by phone, email or online, at any time.
who: Queen Mary staff.
note: Freephone 0800 243 458. No username or password needed.

desc: Free and confidential phone line for anyone who is struggling or needs to talk, every day of the year.
who: Anyone, whatever their age, background or identity.
note: Call 116 123, free from any phone.

desc: Free and confidential text service for people who need mental health support or are in crisis.
who: Anyone in the UK who needs support.
note: Text SHOUT to 85258. If a life is at immediate risk, call 999.

desc: Advice on student mental health, including guides for Black, neurodivergent and trans students. Student Space is now part of this site.
who: University students in the UK.

desc: Information from the charity Mind on mental health problems, where to get help, treatment and advocacy.
who: Anyone looking for information about mental health.
note: Call 0300 123 3393, Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 18:00.

desc: Online resource with research, advice, videos and action plans on wellbeing for postgraduate researchers.
who: Postgraduate research students at any stage.

desc: Queen Mary service that arranges adjustments and support for students with disabilities, dyslexia, ADHD, autism or mental health difficulties.
who: All Queen Mary students, including postgraduate and international students.
note: Call +44 (0)20 7882 2756 or use the online form. Closed on Tuesdays.

desc: Queen Mary online tool to report harassment, sexual violence or hate incidents, with support information and an anonymous option.
who: Any student, employee or visitor at Queen Mary.
note: Anonymous reports do not start a formal process. In an emergency, call 999.

t: QMUL Dignity at Work and Study
desc: Queen Mary policy on bullying, harassment and discrimination, with guidance on how to get advice or report a concern.
who: Students, staff and visitors at Queen Mary.

desc: Free and confidential phone and online chat support for people affected by rape, sexual assault or sexual abuse.
who: Anyone aged 16 or over in England and Wales.

desc: Free helpline run by Refuge for women experiencing domestic abuse, with live chat and BSL options.
who: Women experiencing domestic abuse, and people worried about someone.
note: Call 0808 2000 247. In an emergency, call 999.

desc: Free and confidential legal advice for workers who are worried about wrongdoing at work.
who: Workers in any sector.
note: Call 0203 117 2520, or use the web form.

desc: Free advice on employment rights and problems at work, including disputes, discrimination and bullying.
who: Anyone who needs advice on employment law or work.
note: Call 0300 123 1100, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 18:00. Call charges may apply.

desc: Government-funded helpline with information and advice on discrimination and human rights under equality law.
who: People in Great Britain with a discrimination issue.

desc: LGBT+ anti-abuse charity with helplines for domestic abuse, hate crime and conversion practices.
who: LGBT+ people who have experienced abuse, hate crime or harassment, and people supporting them.
note: Domestic abuse 0800 999 5428. Hate crime 020 7704 2040.
